title: Zipper-Mouth Face Emoji 🤐: “My Lips Are Sealed”
description: 🤐 means “my lips are sealed”: a promise to keep a secret, a decision to hold your tongue, or a blunt “zip it.” See real examples and when it turns rude.
summary: 🤐 has a closed zipper where its mouth should be. It means the sender is keeping quiet: promising not to reveal a secret, choosing not to comment, or biting back an opinion. Aimed at another person, it can also be a blunt “zip it.”
meaning: The emoji illustrates the idiom “zip your lips,” and its friendliest use is a promise. When a friend shares something private, replying 🤐 means the secret is safe. It carries more commitment than a thumbs up because it shows what you will do with the information, which is nothing. People also use it about their own surprises: “I know what your gift is 🤐.”

Just as often it means holding back. “I have thoughts about her new boyfriend but 🤐” tells the reader an opinion exists and is being withheld, usually because it is unkind, controversial or not the sender's business. This is a loud kind of silence. It advertises restraint and invites the other person to ask, which is frequently the point.

It can describe being unable to speak freely. Someone bound by a non-disclosure agreement, a spoiler embargo or a promise to a third party uses 🤐 to say “I know, but I'm not allowed to tell you.” Fans of shows and games use it around leaks and endings, and employees use it when asked about news their company has not announced.

Sent at somebody, the meaning hardens. “🤐” as a reply to a person who is talking too much, spoiling something or arguing is “shut up” in picture form. Among friends that can be a joke. Toward a stranger or in a disagreement it is dismissive, and it tends to escalate things.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It seals confidences and teases withheld information. After “don't tell anyone,” a 🤐 back is the expected answer. It also ends rants the sender decides not to finish: “anyway, I'll stop there 🤐.” When a friend asks what you think and you send only this, they will assume the opinion is negative.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Colleagues use it informally about news that is not public, such as reorganizations, launches or who is leaving. It acknowledges that they know something without disclosing it. Be careful putting that in writing. Hinting that you hold confidential information can itself cause trouble, and the emoji makes the hint obvious.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It appears under spoiler discussions, in teasers for unannounced projects, and in posts where the author signals they are staying out of a controversy. In replies it is also used as a put-down telling another user to stop talking, which is how it most often causes offense.

examples.meaning: A promise not to repeat what was just shared.

examples.text: I saw the finale early. Not saying a word 🤐
examples.meaning: Refusing to give spoilers while letting people know the sender has them.

examples.text: I have opinions about that haircut but 🤐
examples.meaning: Holding back a critical comment, while clearly signaling it exists.

examples.text: Can't talk about the new project yet 🤐
Okay okay, I'll stop giving advice 🤐
examples.meaning: Agreeing, with humor, to stop talking about something.

examples.text: You've said enough for one night 🤐
examples.meaning: Telling someone, playfully or sharply, to be quiet.

combos.meaning: The information is locked away; an emphatic promise of secrecy.
“Lips sealed and I've thrown away the key,” echoing the childhood gesture.
The sender knows something, is not telling, and is watching how things play out.
A request for secrecy followed by agreement; shared confidentiality.

confusedWith.difference: 🤫 asks others to be quiet or teases a secret with a finger to the lips. 🤐 describes the sender's own mouth being shut. 🤫 is “keep this between us”; 🤐 is “I'm not talking.”

😶 has no mouth at all and shows speechlessness, awkward silence or having nothing to say. 🤐 has a mouth that has been deliberately closed, so it implies choice: there is something to say and it is being held in.
🙊 covers its mouth after the fact, as in “oops, I shouldn't have said that,” and is cute and flustered. 🤐 is firmer and more deliberate, a decision to stay silent rather than a reaction to a slip.

avoid: Do not send it at someone during a real argument, because it reads as “shut up” and inflames things.
Avoid hinting at confidential work matters with it in channels that are logged or shared.
Skip it when a friend needs your honest opinion, since visibly withholding it can hurt more than saying it.
design: A yellow face with neutral, open eyes and a horizontal metal zipper, complete with pull tab, in place of the mouth. All major vendors show the zipper fully closed. The differences are small: the zipper may be silver or gray, and the tab sits on the left on some platforms and the right on others.

faqs.a: It is polite when it is about yourself, as in promising secrecy or declining to comment. It is rude when directed at another person as an order to stop talking, unless you are clearly joking with a close friend.

faqs.q: What does 🤐 mean in a text from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually that they are keeping something to themselves: a secret you told them, a surprise, or an opinion they think is better unsaid. If it comes after you asked a direct question, they are dodging it and may open up if you ask again.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🤐 and 😶?
faqs.a: 🤐 is chosen silence: the mouth is zipped on purpose. 😶 is silence from having no words, whether from shock, awkwardness or blankness. One says “I won't speak,” the other “I can't think of anything to say.”

faqs.q: Can 🤐 mean someone is hiding something?
faqs.a: Yes, that is often exactly what it announces. The sender is telling you that information exists and they are not sharing it. Whether that is discreet or annoying depends on whether they were asked to keep it quiet or are just teasing.
The zipper-mouth face was approved in 2015 with 🤔, 🤗, 🙄 and 🤑, part of the first group of new smileys added after emoji became standard on smartphones.
